subject: Request: short-term capacity adjustment and cost-sharing proposal
messages:
From: Emma Park <emma@cloudcart.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@cloudcart.com
Date: Sat, 21 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Short window capacity bump + cost split proposal

Hi Monica,

Quick note from our side — we have a marketing-triggered traffic spike next Thursday through Sunday that will push our token consumption ~2.5x above our committed monthly baseline for a 72-hour window. Our engineering lead flagged potential throttling at ~45 QPS which would materially affect the launch.

We want to avoid a hard outage and are exploring two paths:
- Short-term uplift to our throughput ceiling for the three-day window (we can provide a PO for the incremental headroom), or
- A provisional overrun settlement where CloudCart covers X% of the overage cost and Redwood provides a capped surcharge with a blended unit price.

Procurement copied here — they can issue an interim PO if we can land on a per-token cap and an estimate by EOD Monday. Can you share a quick cost split example and what limits you can guarantee at that volume? Also let us know if Redwood needs a signed amendment or an expedited PO-only path.

Thanks,
Emma Park
Head of Platform Engineering
CloudCart

Attachment: usage_report_Mar2026.csv (3.2 MB) — last 30 days consumption, hourly granularity

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Emma Park <emma@cloudcart.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, procurement@cloudcart.com
Date: Mon, 23 Mar 2026 08:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Short window capacity bump + cost split proposal

Hi Emma — thanks for the heads up and the usage file. We can absolutely support a short, high-throughput window without a full contract rework. A couple of operational notes and two proposed options below.

Operational constraints:
- We can guarantee a throughput ceiling at 120 QPS for the 72-hour window if provisioned 48 hours in advance (warm-up and GPU scheduling).
- If we need to spin additional dedicated capacity within 24 hours, there will be a fast-provision surcharge and degraded SLA for spot routing.

Option A — PO-driven uplift (fastest):
- CloudCart issues an interim PO covering the expected incremental token volume plus a 10% buffer.
- Redwood provides the 120 QPS uplift for the 72-hour window; standard per-token overage rates apply on the incremental usage.
- Estimated uplift cost: $12,000–$15,500 (based on the usage file).

Option B — Cost-share amendment (more predictable):
- Redwood offers a temporary blended overrun rate with a 35% customer share and 65% Redwood concession on the incremental tokens for the 72-hour window.
- Cap the customer-facing surcharge at 1.4x the baseline per-token rate.
- Requires a short amendment (one-page) and a signature; delivery time 24–48 hours.

Next steps:
- If procurement can issue an interim PO today/tomorrow, we’ll proceed with Option A and attach the PO to the provisioning ticket.
- If you prefer Option B, I can circulate the one-page amendment for signature; Ben can propose the final blended numbers by EOD.

I’m CC’ing Ben for precise pricing and Lauren for billing/PO acceptance.

— Monica
Monica Patel
Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachment: proposed_amendment_redlined.docx (stub)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Emma Park <emma@cloudcart.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, procurement@cloudcart.com
Date: Mon, 23 Mar 2026 12:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Short window capacity bump + cost split proposal

Emma — thanks for the usage export, that helped a lot. I modeled expected incremental tokens from 2026-03-25 00:00 – 2026-03-28 23:59 given the hourly peaks you shared. Two concrete numbers for you:

1) PO-driven uplift estimate (Option A): $13,200 (mid-case) — covers expected incremental tokens + 8% buffer.
2) Blended cost-share (Option B): Customer pays $4,620 (35%), Redwood covers $8,580 (65%) — this sets a customer-facing blended rate equal to ~1.3x baseline per-token.

A couple of guardrails I recommend if you take Option B:
- Hard cap on customer liability: $6,000; anything above is absorbed by Redwood for this event only.
- Usage reconciliation after the window (we’ll produce hourly logs and a post-mortem invoice).

If procurement is ready to issue a PO for the Option A amount, we’ll route the ticket to SRE for scheduled provisioning (48-hour lead). If you want Option B, Monica and I will prepare the amendment and DocuSign link.

Ben Carter
Head of Sales, SMB & MidMarket
Redwood Inference

Attachment: CloudCart_overrun_model.xlsx (summary included inline in this message)

From: Emma Park <emma@cloudcart.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@cloudcart.com, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Mar 2026 15:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Short window capacity bump + cost split proposal

Thanks Monica/Ben — appreciate the quick turnaround. Procurement can push an interim PO but prefers to avoid a large one-off if we can get a capped commitment. CloudCart is inclined to accept Option B with the following tweaks:
- We accept the 35% share but request the hard cap be $5,000 instead of $6,000.
- We need a firm written guarantee of 120 QPS for the window with a fallback routing plan if capacity is constrained.
- Please send the amendment and DocuSign link; procurement will countersign once the cap and SLA language are explicit.

If Redwood can agree to the $5k cap and the routing fallback language today, we will sign the amendment and provide the PO as a backup for the provisioning ticket. Otherwise we will issue a PO for Option A by EOD tomorrow.

Best,
Emma Park
Head of Platform Engineering
CloudCart

Attachment: CloudCart_PO_2026-03.pdf (placeholder — procurement will finalize after amendment)
